steps.text: Whisk together the rice vinegar, sesame oil, 3 green onions, garlic, sugar, ginger, soy sauce, vegetable oil, coriander, and mustard in a mixing bowl until the sugar has dissolved. Pour half of the dressing into another container, and refrigerate for later. Place the chicken breasts into the remaining dressing, and coat on all sides. Cover, and refrigerate 30 minutes to 1 hour.
Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Remove the chicken breasts from the marinade, and shake off excess. Discard the remaining marinade. Place the chicken into a baking dish.

Bake the chicken breasts in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 45 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Remove from the oven, and allow to cool. Shred the chicken using 2 forks and set aside.

To assemble the salad, combine the green cabbage, red cabbage, carrots, 3 green onions, cilantro, almonds, and cooled chicken in a large mixing bowl. Pour the reserved dressing overtop and toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Amazing Asian Chicken Salad
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breasts are marinated with ground ginger, coriander, and sesame oil, then roasted and shredded before being added to this colorful Asian-inspired cabbage salad.

review.reviewBody: This was a tasty, colorful salad. Next time I will save more dressing to put on the salad. The chicken was delicious! Easy to put together.

Just made this tonight and we loved it! I added extra chicken and veggies to make it a substantial dinner and DH had 2 full servings! I took another reviewer's idea and threw frozen chicken breasts into the crock pot on high w/1/2 the marinade. After 3 hours I pulled it out, diced it up, and tossed it back in for about 30 minutes to soak up all the juices. It was perfect! I did have to make a little extra sauce b/c of the extra ingredients added, but this was a great recipe! It'll definitely go into our dinner rotation!

Very good and delicious however I thought the dressing would be too strong as sesame oil is very powerful and can overwhelm other flavors- same with the yellow mustard and ginger. I used half of what the recipe called for- 1 tablespoon of sesame oil, 1 teaspoon of mustard, and 1 tablespoon ginger. It turned out a lot better!. I also decreased the amount of cabbage and added romaine lettuce to it- very tasty! And the recipe calls for marinating the meat for 30 min- 1 hour but I did it for 5-6 hours and tasted great!

Really good! This recipe has great flavors. I just made two tiny changes to really knock it out of the park: I cooked the chicken in a covered dutch oven WITH all of the marinade (don't discard it) so that it retains all of that moisture. Then after it's cooked and you shred it, put the shredded chicken back in the dutch oven with the juices and bake for another 15 minutes or so. This will ensure that the chicken is nice and moist and flavorful. The shredded chicken really soaks up those juices. The second change I made was I toasted the almonds in a frying pan until they were a nice golden brown. Delicious!

Turned out great. Only substantive change was using using pre-cooked chicken breasts (from the refrigerated section of your grocery store). I marinated the chicken in the dressing for about 30 minutes, before cutting it into thinner strips and adding it to the salad. Good time saver and a terrific quick recipe.

Used all green cabbage just sliced slivered very thin and added slivered green and yellow bell pepper. I found it easier to julienne the carrots rather than shredding. Used toasted almonds and topped with toasted sesame seeds and crumbled uncooked ramen noodles. This is a fabulous salad, the dressing really makes it! The second time I made the dressing I added one teaspoon of Garam Masala seasoning. Also great with grilled chicken seasoned with teriyaki marinade and just as good with lightly seasoned boiled chicken breast shredded on top when you don't have time for marinating and cooking.

Exactly what you want in an Asian Chicken Salad! The dressing/marinade is so delicious! However I think I may cut back on the ginger next time, it was a bit overwhelming. Only change I made was omitting the green onions due to personal preference. I also added chopped water chestnuts, crushed ramen noodles and sesame seeds. So yummy and easy!
I used fresh ginger in the dressing and made extra so we had plenty for the salad. I also added rice noodles and some peanuts along with the almonds. This was a hit at our house!

Good recipe with Myriah’s tips about cooking the chicken covered in the marinade. Also used half the sesame oil and subbed canola oil for the rest. Didn’t include cilantro. Should have butterflied the chicken; mine came out a little tough. Next time I’ll add salt to the marinade (not the dressing). Nice flavor overall.
I love this, especially when I use my food processor to make it! I skip the sugar entirely, and double the rest of the dressing.

This was delicious! I didn’t have that much ginger so I only put in around 2 tsp but it was still very good and you could taste the ginger. I also am not a huge fan of sesame oil so I only used around 2 tbsp and substituted canola oil for the rest. You could still taste the sesame but it wasn’t strong. I’ll be making this again! Thanks!
This is a great salad. I made extra dressing like others suggested and was happy I did. I also served it with some potstickers to make a nice meal. I will definitely make this again.
Left out the mustard, added half teaspoon of Chili Crunch and it was very good.

With tweaks. HOT Asian Salad. Made as stir fry. Cooked chx all ready sliced to the size I wanted. Then added red onion & coleslaw mix w/little water since I let chx cook to far. Let that start steaming. Added real bacon bits & sauce. No sesame oil so olive oil & sesame seeds instead. No cilantro so oregano instead. Spicy brown mustard. Stuffed breadstix as a side.
It was good. A bit tangy.
This was a delicious salad. The chicken was very moist. Made as noted, also added a few dry Chinese noodles for added crunch.
I didn’t let my family eat this. Not good. The only thing I can think of that I didn’t do exactly is I used dry cilantro and probably not enough. But still- I’m dreading eating the leftovers.
Overall a good recipe, but too much ginger. I added honey peanuts instead of almonds and dried cranberries to boost the flavor.

Made as directed. and took to a "girls' " lunch. The girls enjoyed it, but I found the dressing had something of an off taste, maybe the coriander or the prepared mustard? Probably won't make again because of the problem with the dressing, but can't fault the overall recipe. Thanks, emilyk, for the recipe.

This salad is quite tasty. I left out the coriander, cut down the ginger by half (personal preference) and used powdered mustard, but it was still very good. I rolled these up in flour tortillas for a meal. My husband even liked this! Next time I will double the dressing/marinade, as I felt it was a little dry. Very good flavor though.
